title: Analyze footprint
tagline: Measure any sidecut: dimensions, waist, taper, tip and tail length, average and natural radius, widest and inflection points -- and publish them as variables.

slides.title: What it does
slides.problem: Comparing sidecuts needs the same numbers, measured the same way: tip-waist-tail, taper, radius. Analyze footprint reads them off any outline -- designed, scaled or imported -- and publishes them for later features.
useWhen: Check a sidecut against its targets
Drive later features from measured values
slides.caption: The points it finds: contacts, widest, inflections, waist.

points.head: Average
points.body: Mean of R at 200 X stations between the inflections -- independent of how the edges are split.

points.head: Natural
points.body: One circle through inflection - waist - inflection (or widest - waist - widest).

points.head: They differ
points.body: FX2: 16.97 m average vs 14.47 m natural. Both are right; they answer different questions.

slides.title: The dialog
params: A straight edge FCP to ACP.
Plane, vertex or mate connector; the nearest point on the RSL line is used.
Draw the waist, widest and inflection lines.
Read-only: tip-waist-tail, waist width and X, taper, tip and tail length.
Distances from each contact; inflection to widest.

cards.head: AF1: S14
cards.body: Inflections +-550, average 14.00 m, natural (inflection) 14.00 m, natural (widest) 17.00 m, taper 0.

cards.head: AF2 / AF3: FX2 in 7 or 13 edges
cards.body: Same result either way: average 16.97 m, natural 14.47 m.

keys: Full widths at the widest points and the waist.
World X of the waist; contact to tip / tail end.
Widest to widest; positive when the tip is wider.
messages: Tip-waist-tail ... mm | average radius ... | natural radius (inflection) ...

items.head: Panel goes stale
items.body: The dialog panel updates only when the feature is edited or Recalculate is pressed; the info line and variables are always current.

items.head: Any orientation along X
items.body: Tip at +X and off-centre skis measure correctly (AF4, AF5); raw sketch arcs too (AF7).
